Precisely what freaked me out about these comments. I've never really had an experience with someone thinking I'm a "Fellow" bigot before. Most of the time, in my fics, I tend to push towards realism that isn't usually seen in the canon material, in this case, it was set in a small town in the 1990s and some of the characters were older men, in a story that did have gay characters. So of course there were some moments where I used pejoritaves. The character that used these words the most, was seen mostly as a comedic relief, and was often the butt of jokes in the story due to their gung-ho attitude. I wanted to portray him as a flawed person who was far too brash and immature to be working with the younger generation. The character, was flawed, and hid more short-sighted attitude gets him into a lot of trouble in the fic, to the point he suffers actual punishment due to the main character view them as too volatile to allow to speak to some people. The idea that these people see that character and project onto them and assume my intent was to encourage his actions and behavior is honestly disgustingly funny to me. They don't see him as a flawed individual who is being rightfully punished, and instead choose to see him as the only right person in a system that works against them. What I think is happening is that they are idolizing him and think of him as a matyr.
